evidence: run c5t27_s367941497: object first seen at t=0.12 s (1.93 m) but collision with mover_00 occurs at t=5.0 s despite an early stop at t=0.2 s
run c5t27_s1661556862: first unmapped point within 2 m at t=40.15 s, collision with mover_03 at t=45.083 s (≈5 s later) after the clearance hold timed out
run c5t27_s603735424: stall abort at t=122.45 s after many stop‑turn episodes; robot moved only 0.292 m in the last 60 s, indicating it could not resume after repeated stops

assumptions.assumption: Robot can safely resume once the nearest unmapped point and any tracked mover are > _CLEAR_R (2 m) away for at least _CLEAR_OK_T (0.5 s)
assumptions.why: Collisions happen after the hold ends while the object is still within ~2 m (e.g., runs 2 and 4)

assumptions.assumption: A fixed maximum clearance‑hold duration (_CLEAR_MAX = 4 s) is sufficient for any moving object to clear the safety zone
assumptions.why: Both collisions occur >4 s after the first detection, showing the fixed cap is too short

assumptions.assumption: When a mover is inside _SAFE_DIST, the VO planner will always find a safe trajectory within its horizon
assumptions.why: Several runs show the VO planner returns None, after which the controller falls back to predictive speed and collides

approach_families.family: VO‑based planning (including synthetic tracks, VO‑only, VO+detour, etc.)

candidates.idea: Adaptive clearance hold: compute time‑to‑collision (TTC) from _dynamic_pause or _raw_ttc_stop and keep the robot stopped until TTC exceeds a safe threshold (e.g., 2 s) instead of a fixed 4 s cap
candidates.for: collisions after the fixed hold expires while the object is still nearby
candidates.risk: Longer stops may increase overall mission time; TTC estimation errors could cause unnecessary delays

candidates.idea: Remove predictive‑speed fallback after a stop; if VO planner cannot produce a safe command, keep the robot stopped (or rotate in place) until a safe command appears
candidates.for: preventing unsafe forward motion when VO fails
candidates.risk: May cause stalls if VO cannot find a path for an extended period

candidates.idea: Prioritize side‑detour generation after any stop: when _min_gap ≤ _SAFE_DIST and VO fails, immediately invoke _side_detour with a larger lateral offset and longer timeout
candidates.for: providing a deterministic escape route when VO is unable to plan
candidates.risk: Side detour may conflict with static obstacles, requiring additional map checks

diagnosis.chosen: Adaptive clearance hold (candidate A) is selected because the fixed 4 s maximum hold is insufficient; extending the hold dynamically based on actual TTC ensures the robot only resumes when the moving object is truly safe.
diagnosis.direction: 1. Add constants _CLEAR_TTC = 2.0 and _CLEAR_TTC_MARGIN = 0.5. 2. In _arm_clear_hold compute the current TTC using _dynamic_pause (or _raw_ttc_stop) and set st["clear_hold_until"] = t + max(_CLEAR_TTC, ttc + _CLEAR_TTC_MARGIN). 3. Modify _clear_hold to drop the fixed _CLEAR_MAX cap and keep holding while min(d, gap) ≤ _CLEAR_R or TTC < _CLEAR_TTC. 4. Remove the grace‑period logic that releases the hold after a fixed time; instead release only after the TTC‑based condition is satisfied for _CLEAR_OK_T seconds. 5. Ensure every place that calls _arm_clear_hold passes the current M (track array) so TTC can be evaluated. 6. Test that after a stop the robot remains halted until the moving object’s TTC exceeds the threshold, then resumes normal VO/predictive‑speed control.
